description: Former Vice President of the United States, Mike Pence, shares his thoughts about President Trump's framework on trying to acquire Greenland, and discusses what he is disappointed about when it comes to Trump's Board of Peace. Pence also states that he is hopeful the US Supreme Court will overturn Trump's tariff policies. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hopeful SCOTUS Will Overturn Trump Tariffs: Mike Pence

author: Natalia Drozdiak, Joe Deaux
description: The US wants to rewrite its defense agreement with Denmark to remove any limits on its military presence in Greenland, people familiar with the matter said, in what’s become a focal point for negotiators looking to meet President Donald Trump’s demand for control over the territory.
title: US Seeks Carte Blanche for Military Presence in Greenland

author: James Mayger
description: China will set a lower economic growth target range for 2026 than last year, the South China Morning Post reported, reflecting mounting signs that activity will continue to slow.
title: China Will Set Lower Growth Target as Economy Slows, SCMP Says

author: Catherine Lucey
description: Donald Trump has imposed more tariffs than any American president in at least a century – but only a fraction of the ones he’s threatened.
title: Trump’s Tariffs Do Bite — When He Actually Imposes Them

description: Wall Street and corporate America are facing a delicate dance at the start of 2026: How do you help clients and shareholders reckon and prepare themselves for Trump’s policy onslaught without drawing his ire? Increasingly, the answer is self-censorship. As leaders contend with an onslaught of policy announcements and changes, coupled with major geopolitical shifts, the decision of what to say and when to say it is as important as decision-making itself. Alan Guarino, Vice Chairman of Korn Ferry, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. Guarino also promotes his new book, “Greatness Code: The Formula Behind Unstoppable Success." He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: CEOs Navigate Waterfall of Trump Policy Shifts

description: US airlines are already announcing backup plans for passengers ahead of an expected winter storm this weekend that could be the biggest of the season and cause massive disruptions to air traffic nationwide. Delta Air Lines is offering rebooking for flights to and from 41 airports across the South and Southeast, including its main hub in Atlanta as well as Dallas, Austin, Houston, Charleston and Memphis. Passengers will be allowed to make new plans without paying a fare difference until Jan. 28, the airline said on its website. United Airlines will waive change fees and fare differences for flights impacted from 61 airports, including East Coast cities such as Boston, Newark and New York’s La Guardia. Bloomberg News Chief Correspondent for Global Aviation Siddharth Philip joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Airlines Offer to Waive Fees Ahead of Big Winter Storm

author: Hadriana Lowenkron, Randall Williams
description: Commissioners from top US men’s pro sports leagues are expected to visit the White House as early as next week to discuss President Donald Trump’s plans for celebrating America’s 250th anniversary, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Trump to Host NFL, NBA for Planning America’s 250th Birthday

author: Josh Wingrove, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump said he has finished interviewing candidates to serve as the next Federal Reserve chair and reiterated that he has someone in mind for the job.
title: Trump Says Fed Chair Interviews Are Done, Has Pick in Mind

author: Hadriana Lowenkron, Katy O'Donnell
description: President Donald Trump threw cold water on a policy his administration was developing to allow savers in 401(k) retirement plans to use some of that money for down payments on homes — a proposal that had been a key part of his efforts to address voters’ affordability concerns.
title: Trump Undercuts Plan to Let Homebuyers Tap Retirement Plans

description: The former Justice Department official who secured indictments against Donald Trump told lawmakers that the president is unfairly seeking retribution against prosecutors and FBI agents who worked on his investigations. “President Trump has sought to seek revenge against career prosecutors, FBI agents and support staff, simply for having worked on these cases,” former Special Counsel Jack Smith said during his first time testifying publicly about his sweeping investigations. Smith brought charges against Trump for allegedly trying to overturn the 2020 election and mishandling classified information. Bloomberg News Justice Department Reporter Chris Strohm joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Jack Smith Tells Congress Trump Is Seeking Revenge Over Charges

author: Erik Wasson, Ken Tran
description: The Republican-controlled House overwhelmingly passed annual funding measures Thursday reversing some of Donald Trump’s most controversial federal spending cuts, including restoring money for medical research, refugee assistance and even the Department of Education.
title: GOP-Controlled House Passes 2026 Funding Reversing Key Trump Cuts

author: Sam Dagher
description: As the country recovers from the disastrous US invasion, it’s being pulled between its neighbor Iran, which has built decades of influence, and a president who wants America to have more sway in OPEC’s second-largest producer.
title: Torn Between Iran and Trump, Iraq Confronts a Stark Choice

description: The Supreme Court seemed wary of Trump’s bid to fire Federal Reserve Board Governor Lisa Cook in a hearing on Wednesday. Bloomberg reporters Amara Omeokwe and Greg Stohr break down arguments from both sides of the case and analyze key reactions from justices on the bench: Listen to the Big Take podcast. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why the Cook Outcome Will Matter for Fed Independence

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss today's economic data with Bloomberg's Mike McKee, including stronger-than-expected GDP and steadying jobless claims. Then, Ark Invest CEO and CIO Cathie Wood joins the program to discuss her “Big Ideas 2026” report and why she's still focusing on Tesla, AI and health care stocks. Plus, Alan Guarino, Vice Chairman of Korn Ferry, on his new book, “Greatness Code: The Formula Behind Unstoppable Success” and how CEOs are navigating President Trump's policy announcements as they make appearances at the World Economic Forum. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Climb on Solid Data, Global Tensions Cool | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 1/22/2026

author: Erik Wasson
description: Funding bill let Democrats make a statement without creating a standoff.
title: Democrats Get ICE Protest Vote But Shy Away From Forcing a Shutdown

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the conclusion of President Donald Trump's trip to the World Economic Forum in Davos. On today's show, House Homeland Security Committee Chairman Andrew Garbarino of New York, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and US Army Transformation and Training Command Executive Director Joseph Welch. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Meets Zelenskiy at Davos | Balance of Power: Early Edition 1/22/2026

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: Vice President JD Vance argued that tensions in Minnesota over immigration enforcement operations could be tamed if local and state officials cooperated more with US authorities, even as he conceded federal officers sometimes make “mistakes.”
title: Vance Nods at ICE Errors, Blames Minnesota Leaders for Chaos

description:
Cathie Wood, Founder, CEO and CIO of Ark Invest, said that investment in data centers needs to ramp up significantly to $1.4 trillion in the next five years to support the AI boom. 
Wood also discussed the impact of AI on the job market, saying she's not concerned with disruption and arguing that AI will create 'new worlds' of job creation in the future.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Data Center Spending Needs to Be at $1.4 Trillion in Next 5 Years, Says Cathie Wood

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russian President Vladimir Putin began talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in the Kremlin on the latest peace plan aimed at ending his war in Ukraine.
title: Putin Starts Moscow Talks With US Envoys Witkoff and Kushner

author: Michelle Kaske
description: Public transportation systems across the US are poised to get a $100.3 million assist from the federal government as Congress considers directing more money to transit agencies in cities that are hosting this year’s FIFA World Cup games.
title: Congress Set to Give Transit Systems $100 Million for World Cup

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: Senator Amy Klobuchar has filed paperwork to explore a run for Minnesota governor just weeks after fellow Democrat Tim Walz announced he would not seek another term, people close to the senator said.
title: Klobuchar Files Paperwork to Explore Minnesota Governor Run

description: Joseph Welch, executive director of US Army Transformation and Training Command, said that AI can help soldiers do their jobs better and help them make 'human based judgments consistent with our laws and our values' when they're out in the field. Welch said that the Army's goal is to rapidly advance the state of their technology and that he's seeing support for 'once in a generation change.'  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Army Explores Future of AI in Warfare

description: Former Special Counsel Jack Smith, who secured indictments against Donald Trump, told lawmakers that the president is unfairly seeking retribution against prosecutors and FBI agents who worked on his investigations during his first time testifying publicly. Chris Strohm has more. (Corrects to add Smith is former Special Counsel.) (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Jack Smith Defends Trump Investigations Before Congress

author: Ellen Milligan, James Woolcock, Alex Wickham
description: Keir Starmer is bracing for a potential showdown with a key left-wing rival in a test of the British prime minister’s power to stave off the gathering threats to his job.
title: Starmer Girds for Showdown to Block Rival Burnham From Commons

description: House Homeland Security Committee Chair Andrew Garbarino said Greenland can serve as important as a check on Russia and China in the Arctic and it's important for the US to work with NATO in meeting that challenge. Garbarino also discussed the looming government funding deadline and warned about the impacts of a block against homeland security funding in the wake of discord in Minneapolis.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Greenland Can Serve as Check on Russia, China 'Aggressiveness' in Arctic, Says Garbarino

description: Greenland is willing to have a larger NATO presence on the Arctic island, but there are red lines that can't be crossed, says Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen. He speaks in Danish territory's capital of Nuuk. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Greenland Is Willing to Let NATO Have a Larger Presence, Prime Minister Says

author: Josh Saul
description: New York regulators adopted an agreement between Consolidated Edison Inc. and other parties that would limit the utility’s revenues — and cap increases to customer bills — for the next three years, according to a news release Thursday.
title: New York Cuts ConEd’s Rate Request by 85%, Citing Affordability

author: Thomas Escritt
description: Hungary’s Prime Minister Viktor Orban reacted with an angry post on his social media platforms after Volodymyr Zelenskiy accused him of acting against European interests.
title: Hungary’s Orban Bristles at Zelenskiy’s ‘Little Moscow’ Jab

author: Jorge Valero
description: European Union lawmakers are expected to vote on ratifying the bloc’s trade deal with the US, restarting the process after President Donald Trump walked back his latest threat to impose tariffs on European allies that opposed his plans to annex Greenland.
title: EU Plans to Unfreeze Trade Deal With US and Vote on Ratification

author: Patricia Laya
description: The US named two-time Ambassador Laura Dogu as its new chargé d’affaires for Venezuela, signaling a rapid push to reestablish a formal diplomatic presence in Caracas.
title: US Names Diplomat to Venezuela to Rebuild Ties After Trump Raid

author: Suzanne Lynch
description: European officials agreed on one thing in the hours after US President Donald Trump pulled back from the brink over Greenland: The continent’s economy and defenses must stand on their own, fast.
title: Shellshocked EU Rethinks US Relationship After Trump Threat

description: Earlier this week, we saw something unusual happen in markets. The S&P 500 fell 2%, US Treasury yields rose, and the dollar simultaneously declined. This trifecta of markets moves has rekindled talk of the "Sell America" trade as investors worry about the Trump administrations threats to take over Greenland. At the same time, Japanese bonds sold off after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called a snap election. So how concerned should investors be about these latest developments? Is the "Sell America" trade really back? Or are we seeing a global rise in long bond yields? In this episode we talk with Pimco CEO Manny Roman about how he’s reading the moves. We also discuss Pimco's investment in data center debt, how the company is using AI internally, and why he doesn't 'get' gold. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pimco CEO Manny Roman on Japanese Bonds and the Sell America Trade

author: Madlin Mekelburg
description: The California Republican Party asked the US Supreme Court to block the state from using its new congressional map that favors Democrats during this year’s midterm election.
title: Supreme Court Asked by GOP to Block New California Voting Map

description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy says he thinks President Donald Trump can talk to Russia's Vladimir Putin and end the war in Ukraine. Zelenskiy spoke to reporters on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Can End the War With Russia, Ukraine's Zelenskiy Says

author: Will Standring
description: If Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham wants to mount a leadership challenge against UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer he faces a number of obstacles that make for a tricky route to power.
title: Andy Burnham Faces Tortuous Path to Challenge UK’s Starmer

author: John Tozzi, Caitlin Reilly
description: Lawmakers pointed the finger at insurance executives for high US health costs in a hearing Thursday, as Congress seeks to deflect blame for a health system that’s become unaffordable to many Americans.
title: Lawmakers Grill Health CEOs on Costs as ACA Hangs Over Debate

description:
Gautam Mukunda, Lecturer at Yale School of Management and Bloomberg Opinion contributor joins to recap Trump's Davos visit and his dropping of Greenland tariffs for now. President Donald Trump said he would refrain from imposing tariffs on goods from European nations opposing his effort to take possession of Greenland, citing a “framework of a future deal” he said was reached regarding the island. 

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney declared during his Davos speech that recent events have shown the “rules-based international order” is effectively dead, and that other countries must forge new partnerships to withstand pressure tactics from great powers. French President Emmanuel Macron said Trump’s trade strategy is meant to “weaken and subordinate Europe.” Belgian Prime Minister Bart de Wever said he no longer considers the US an ally. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Impossible To Overstate The Damage The  US Has Done To Allies Says Mukunda

author: Christian Wienberg
description: Greenland’s prime minister says he’s willing to go further in increasing the defense of the Arctic island coveted by President Donald Trump, including agreeing on the establishment of a permanent NATO mission.
title: Greenland Leader Open to Permanent NATO Mission on Arctic Island

author: David Voreacos, Hannah Levitt
description: President Donald Trump sued JPMorgan Chase & Co. and its chief executive officer, Jamie Dimon, for at least $5 billion over allegations that the lender stopped offering him and his businesses banking services for political reasons.
title: Trump Sues JPMorgan for $5 Billion Over Debanking Claims

author: Ignacio Olivera Doll, Walter Brandimarte
description: Since taking office in 2023, Javier Milei has had to adapt many of his radical ideas to the realities of governing Argentina. Chinese officials he once called “assassins” turned into “great trade partners.” The central bank he pledged to burn down is still standing. Talk of dollarization has ceased.
title: Milei Doesn't Think Argentina Is Ready for a Free-Floating Peso Yet

author: Katherine Doherty, Todd Gillespie
description: Bank of America Corp. and Citigroup Inc. are exploring options they could offer up as an olive branch to satisfy President Donald Trump’s demand to cap credit card interest rates at 10% for one year.
title: Bank of America, Citigroup Weigh New Credit Cards With 10% Rate

author: Chris Strohm
description: The former Justice Department official who secured indictments against Donald Trump told lawmakers that the president is unfairly seeking retribution against prosecutors and FBI agents who worked on his investigations.
title: Jack Smith Tells Congress Trump Is Seeking Revenge Over Charges

description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy accused European allies of failing to halt Russia’s actions and lacking the will to act as a real global power. He addressed the World Economic Forum in Davos on Thursday. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy Says Europe Isn't Doing Enough to End War With Russia

author: Prinesha Naidoo
description: South Africa’s International Trade Administration Commission plans to review the reference price for sugar amid a flood of imports crippling local producers.
title: South Africa to Revisit Sugar-Price Trigger After Import Surge

author: Fabiola Zerpa, Andreina Itriago
description: Venezuela is set to debate a proposal on Thursday that would allow private oil companies to commercialize their own production, pay less in taxes and settle disputes through arbitration, rather than exclusively in Venezuelan courts, according to a draft bill seen by Bloomberg.
title: Venezuela to Debate Oil Bill Allowing Private Sales, Arbitration

author: Beatriz Reis
description: Brazil’s tax collection hit a record high in 2025 according to data published on Thursday, giving President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva greater room to raise public spending during his reelection bid this year.
title: Brazil Tax Revenues Surge to Record, Giving Lula Spending Leeway

description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said his nation needs US involvement in any postwar security guarantees as he criticized Europe's lack of action and for continuing to rely on Russian energy supplies. "That oil helps destabilize Europe," Zelenskiy explained during a speech at the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland. "If [Russian President Vladimir] Putin has no money, there is no war for Europe. If Europe has money, then it can protect its people," he added. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy Criticizes Europe's Lack of Action

author: Ellen DiMauro
description: US Senator Elizabeth Warren and three other Senate Democrats are asking Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to launch a probe into large debt packages supporting artificial intelligence and the risks they pose to the financial system.
title: Bessent Urged by Warren to Probe ‘Opaque’ Data Center Financings

author: Daryna Krasnolutska, Aliaksandr Kudrytski
description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy tore into Europe for its apparent lack of willingness to stop Vladimir Putin as his country endures devastating Russian missile and drone attacks on water, heating and power networks in freezing winter temperatures.
title: Zelenskiy Blasts Europe for Inaction in Countering Putin

description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto predicted that growth will accelerate this year as he touted his policy program for Southeast Asia’s biggest economy to the business elite in Davos.

description: France’s navy boarded an oil tanker coming from Russia into the Mediterranean Sea, as part of a global crackdown on shadow fleet used to export sanctioned crude.
title: France Boards Russia-Linked Oil Tanker in Shadow Fleet Move

description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto speaks at the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland. He says the country's economy "grew by more than 5% every year over the last decade" and adds that he is confident growth in 2026 "will be higher." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Prabowo Says Indonesia's Growth in 2026 'Will Be Higher'

description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick says relationships with our European allies and others are fine. He also talks about the security agreements reached about Greenland on "Bloomberg Surveillance" at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lutnick Says Relations With Europe, Greenland Are Fine

description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick dismissed as “political noise” the moves in recent days by Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney to strengthen trade relations with China, and raised the risk of that maneuver seeping into talks over a revamped North American trade accord later this year.
title: Lutnick Dismisses Canada Tilt to China, Sees Summer USMCA Talks

description: A judge ruled that a New York congressional district must be redrawn, giving Democrats an opportunity to pick up another seat in Congress ahead of November’s hotly-contested midterm elections.
title: NYC’s Only Republican Seat Must Be Redrawn, Helping Democrats

description: In a conflict-ravaged Middle East, a deep and stable relationship between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates has endured for decades.

title: Milei at Davos Hails Argentina’s China Ties in Defense of Trade

description: Argentina's President Javier Milei discusses the capture of Nicolás Maduro and the Trump administration's plan for Venezuela. He speaks to Bloomberg Editor-in-Chief John Micklethwait at Bloomberg House on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: UK Move to Delay 29 Local Elections Angers Opposition Parties

title: Iran Protest Deaths Seen Rising With One Estimate Topping 20,000

description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, easily survived a no-confidence vote in the European Parliament that far-right lawmakers pushed over a recent trade deal with South American countries.
title: EU’s Von der Leyen Survives Fourth No-Confidence Vote

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day.

On today's show, President Donald Trump said he would refrain from imposing tariffs on goods from European nations opposing his effort to take possession of Greenland, citing a “framework of a future deal” he said was reached
regarding the island.

Stocks climbed after Donald Trump backed off his threats of imposing tariffs on European nations opposing his efforts to take control of Greenland.

Vladimir Putin said he’s ready to commit frozen Russian assets to rebuild Ukrainian regions after a peace treaty is concluded. He also floated the idea of giving the money to Trump’s Board of Peace.

Today's guests: Elina Ribakova, Nonresident Senior Fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics and Director of the International Affairs Programme at Kyiv School of Economics & Engie CEO Catherine MacGregor (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Greenland’s sovereignty, a red line for Denmark, wasn’t discussed.

description: South Africa’s government is appealing for donations to help fund repairs at the iconic Kruger National Park, following torrential rains and flooding that claimed dozens of lives and caused widespread damages to lodges, camps and roads.
title: South Africa Seeks Donations to Repair Kruger Park Flood Damage

author: Magdalena Del Valle, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump officially launched his Board of Peace initiative, barreling ahead with a project he says will promote geopolitical stability even as its creation spurs rancor and reservations from key allies.
title: Trump Launches His Board of Peace Despite Discord From Allies

author: Francine Lacqua, William Horobin
description: France’s minister for trade, Nicolas Forissier, slammed Donald Trump’s threats to slap tariffs on champagne and repeated pledges to retaliate if the US president ever followed through.
title: France Says Trump Must Stop Threatening Champagne Tariffs

author: Erica Yokoyama
description: Less than a month after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said the nation was set to achieve its first primary balance surplus in 28 years, the latest official estimates indicate that her recent stimulus package has knocked the government off track.
title: Takaichi’s Extra Spending Knocks Japan Off Budget Surplus Track

description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said a breakthrough over Greenland was achieved by focusing on the broader issue of security in the Arctic region. The discussion with US President Donald Trump centered on regional security in a "practical sense," he told Bloomberg News Editor-in-Chief John Micklethwait. Speaking in an interview at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, Rutte also discussed the situation in Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Greenland Talks Avoided Sovereignty, Rutte Says

description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the foundations of the international order "have been shaken" and that nations shouldn't "accept this new reality as fate." He made the comments during a speech at the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland. "We do not have to accept this new reality as fate," Merz added. "We are not at the mercy of this new world order. We do have a choice. We can shape the future." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Germany's Merz: 'We Are Not at the Mercy of This New World Order'

author: William Clowes, Antony Sguazzin
description: White farmers in Zimbabwe, thousands of whom had their land seized in violent state-backed invasions beginning in 2000, are pinning their hopes on US President Donald Trump’s administration to help them win billions of dollars in compensation.
title: White Zimbabwe Farmers Turn to Trump in $3.5 Billion Dispute

author: Michael Nienaber, Arne Delfs
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe needs to boost its unity and competitiveness in order to fight back against a new era of “great-power politics” that’s upended the transatlantic relationship.
title: Merz Calls for European Unity to Defend Against Power Politics

author: Andrea Palasciano
description: NATO’s chief said a breakthrough over Greenland was secured without discussing the territory’s sovereignty with President Donald Trump, focusing rather on the broader issue of security in the Arctic region.
title: Rutte Says Trump Greenland Talks Avoided Sovereignty Issue

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is set to face two more impeachment complaints at the House of Representatives, underscoring growing political tensions even as the efforts may falter in a congress dominated by his allies.
title: Marcos Faces Three Impeachment Bids in a Week as Philippine Politics Heats Up

description: California Governor Gavin Newsom said he was denied entry to an event at the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos after pressure from the White House. Newsom had been invited to speak at an event at the USA House, a venue showcasing US companies at Davos, his office said in a post on X. “Is it surprising the Trump administration didn’t like my commentary and wanted to make sure that I was not allowed to speak? No. It’s consistent with this administration and their authoritarian tendenc
title: Newsom Says White House Barred Him From Davos Event

author: Nectar Gan, Colum Murphy
description: Japan’s diplomatic mission in the southwestern Chinese megacity of Chongqing has been left without a consul-general, as relations between Tokyo and Beijing remain strained.
title: Japan’s Chongqing Consulate Lacks Top Envoy Amid China Tensions

author: Fred Ojambo
description: Uganda’s main opposition party said one of its top officials had been arrested by security operatives, the third to be detained since last week’s election that handed President Yoweri Museveni a seventh term.
title: Top Ugandan Opposition Officials Arrested After Disputed Vote

author: Daryna Krasnolutska
description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy is on his way to Davos to meet with Donald Trump on Thursday, according to a person familiar with the matter.
title: Ukraine President Zelenskiy Heads to Davos to Meet With Trump

author: Andrew Atkinson, Philip Aldrick
description: UK government borrowing fell more than expected in December, helping Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves in her bid to bring the public finances under control.
title: UK Budget Deficit Narrowed More Than Forecast in December

author: John Harney, Anthony Capaccio
description: The aircraft that Qatar donated to the US as a new Air Force One for President Donald Trump could be delivered in the next several months.
title: Summer Delivery Seen for Qatari Jet Trump Wants as Air Force One

author: Anisah Shukry
description: Malaysia is reviewing its rules for regulating social media platforms after an outcry over sexualized images of people generated by Elon Musk’s Grok artificial intelligence chatbot.
title: Malaysia Weighs Social Media Rule Change After Grok AI Uproar

author: Manolo Serapio Jr
description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was advised by his doctors to rest, having spent the night under medical observation after experiencing discomfort, his office said on Thursday.
title: Philippines’ Marcos Advised by Doctors to Rest After Discomfort

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: South Korea isn’t delaying the first planned $20 billion tranche of its US investment commitments as part of a trade deal framework, Finance Minister Koo Yun Cheol said, adding that the time-consuming process to select projects is underway even though it’s unlikely to be completed in the first half of the year.
title: South Korea Says It’s Not Delaying $20 Billion US Investment

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Retired General Wesley Clark, former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe, discusses President Trump not imposing Greenland tariffs as the President suggests a framework deal between the US & NATO's Mark Rutte. Frank Luntz, Fil Inc. Founder & West Point Professor, talks about what President Trump's messaging needs to be as the 2026 Midterm election campaign seasons starts. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Announces 'Framework' Of A Deal On Greenland | Balance of Power: Late Edition 01/21/2026

author: Tracy Withers
description: New Zealand annual immigration continues to show signs of a tentative recovery, with revised data showing the recent exodus of citizens was smaller than first thought.
title: New Zealand Immigration Rising as Kiwi Exodus Revised Lower

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: US Senator Richard Blumenthal is demanding answers from the Department of Homeland Security after whistle blowers disclosed a new policy that he claimed would let immigration agents enter homes without a judge’s warrant to carry out civil immigration arrests.
title: Democratic Senator Blasts ‘Secret’ ICE Policy to Enter Homes

author: Alex Wickham
description: British business leaders want the governing Labour Party to keep under-pressure Keir Starmer as prime minister, but many are open to the prospect of backing Nigel Farage’s Reform UK at the next election, a survey found.
title: British Business Leaders Say Keep Starmer But Flirt With Farage
